A ray of light originates from point \(A\) and travels in a plane, being reflected \(n\) times between lines \(AD\) and \(CD,\) before striking a point \(B\) (which may be on \(AD\) or \(CD\)) perpendicularly and retracing its path to \(A.\) (At each point of reflection the light makes two equal angles as indicated in the adjoining figure. The figure shows the light path for \(n=3.\)) If \(\angle CDA=8^\circ,\) what is the largest value \(n\) can have?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

In triangle \(ABC\) in the adjoining figure, \(AD\) and \(AE\) trisect \(\angle BAC.\) The lengths of \(BD,\) \(DE,\) and \(EC\) are \(2,\) \(3,\) and \(6,\) respectively. The length of the shortest side of \(\triangle ABC\) is
